function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Out of the 20-call budget with the block still on the table. The last close at (x=-0.148, y=0.034, z=0.832) pinched air again (gripper read 0.0162 = fully closed), and a grasp needs one more descend-and-close cycle which the budget no longer allows. The task (block inside bowl) is not achieved.", "hindsight": "Key rig facts learned: (1) The move tool only executes a long, fully-tracked motion when the call includes a gripper latch change (open/close swing); commands without one are cut to 1-2 control steps (~2-5 mm), which makes positioning extremely slow. Include a gripper swing (or gripper=0.5 retain trick while carrying) as fuel so the interpolation runs ~80 steps / 4 s, covering ~2-4 cm of Cartesian travel. (2) Initial pose: gripper open-loop above the table at x=-0.124, y=0.001, z=1.004. The red block sits near (-0.145, +0.02) with its top at z~0.835 (table z=0.80); the blue bowl is ~20 cm further in +y at x~-0.135, so the whole place is far in +y. (3) Wrist camera is tilted and rolled: world +x maps to image-down in the wrist view (verified: +3.2 cm x move shifted the block +19 px down, scale ~0.6 px/mm at z=1.0), image-right maps to -y; the block reads image-centered in both axes when the hand is still ~1-2 cm short in x and a couple cm off in y, so do not trust centering alone. (4) The gripper pad flat faces sit roughly 2 cm above the tapered finger tips, and the tips hang ~3 cm below the eef; a side grasp therefore needs eef z~0.82-0.83 (tips just above the table) before closing, and the close must happen at that height. (5) Measured gripper 0.0162 = closed empty; a held 3.5 cm block would read ~0.4-0.5. (6) The arm tracks ~85% of large commanded moves; the descent reached 10 cm in one call near the table."}
